title: TraceQA heal
description: The result of `traceqa heal RUN --against BASELINE`: healing as a query over a diff. Every component of the baseline that the run does not have as it was is classified once. Identity-preserving drift (the same id, another way to find it) is a mechanical fix. A rename is only ever a proposal for a person to accept. A removal is a failure, an unclear match is refused, and a run that was signed out heals nothing. Heals never change the baseline's components: `traceqa baseline promote` stays the only way to move the reference.

HealReport.description: heal.json, written to the run folder, and the output of `traceqa heal --format json`. Fully determined by the run, the baseline and the --accept choices; the items are ordered by target, then kind, then id.

items.description: One per baseline component that is not present as it was. Components that are unchanged are only counted in the summary.

HealItem.description: What to do about one baseline component.

id.description: The component id in the baseline. Empty for session_not_accepted, which concerns the whole run.

newId.description: The component id in the run, for rename_proposal and locator_fix (the same id).

target.description: The target folder this was found in, for example chromium-1280x800.

name.description: The component's name in the baseline.

confidence.description: For rename_proposal only: high when both sides carry the same data-testid, medium when the evidence is the name and the position.

evidence.description: Why, one sentence each. For ambiguous, the candidates.

fixPreview.description: For locator_fix and rename_proposal: the locator as Playwright TypeScript before and after, in the form `- old` newline `+ new`.

accepted.description: True when --accept recorded this proposal as an alias in the baseline in this run of the command.

HealKind.description: locator_fix: same id, another locator. rename_proposal: removed here, one probable new id. removed: gone, no candidate. ambiguous: more than one candidate on a side. session_not_accepted: the run was signed out. unchanged: present as it was (only in library results, never listed in a report).

HealAction.description: fix: a mechanical change that is safe to apply. propose: a person has to decide. fail: a failure to fix in the product or the baseline. refuse: not enough to decide. none: nothing to do.

accepted.description: Proposals recorded as aliases by --accept in this run of the command.

failed.description: True when the command exits 1: any item whose action is not none or fix, or a proposal that was not accepted.
